answer: Retrospective behavioral correlation. Agents are scored by the statistical thread of their recorded actions: timing correlations, shared transaction sequences, and overlapping counterparties. New identities that later correlate above threshold with an existing cluster get merged and downweighted retroactively. A cedar audit trail of signed events makes cluster evidence durable. Cost: an attacker must sustain independent falcon-like precision across many identities for months, and detected clusters forfeit accumulated reputation.
